prompt: Some people think young people should be required to have full time education until they are at least 18 years old. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often argued that youngsters should be required to remain in full-time education until they reach the age of 18. I completely agree with this view, given that prolonged education not only provides adolescents with a stronger academic foundation, but also helps them to make more informed career decisions for the future.

The first major reason why young people should remain in education until the age of 18 is that it gives them sufficient time to obtain essential academic and social skills. Subjects, such as mathematics, chemistry and languages provide students with knowledge that may be applied to both career and higher education. Furthermore, those years help them to develop critical thinking, problem-solving and communication skills. For example, a pupil who continues studying mathematics and English tends to solve practical problems and express ideas easily. Therefore, compulsory education can substantially improve their academic and professional prospects.

Another compelling argument in favour of this view is that extending education can prevent learners from making premature career decisions. Teenagers often have limited information about the labour market and have not discovered their own strengths and interests. If they leave school too early, they may accept low-skilled jobs, thereby having several difficulties, say not adapting to the working environment or insufficient income. For example, in his mid-teens juvenile can work in any unskilled position, but his status and qualifications may remain restricted or limited, whereas two additional years of education may allow them to explore different subjects and identify a profession that genuinely suits their abilities. As a result, they can make exact and well-informed decisions about their future.

To conclude, I completely agree that young people should be required to remain in full-time education until the age of 18.
